paragraphs.en: “The ancient Hawaiians were astronomers,” wrote Queen Liliuokalani, Hawaii’s last reigning monarch, in 1897. Star watchers were among the most esteemed members of Hawaiian society. Sadly, all is not well with astronomy in Hawaii today. Protests have erupted over construction of the Thirty Meter Telescope (TMT), a giant observatory that promises to revolutionize humanity’s view of the cosmos.
paragraphs.zh: 夏威夷最后一位在位君主利留卡拉尼女王于1897年写道：“古代夏威夷人是天文学家。”观星者曾是夏威夷社会中最受尊敬的成员之一。遗憾的是，如今夏威夷的天文学发展并不顺利。围绕三十米望远镜的建设，抗议活动已经爆发。这座巨型天文台有望彻底改变人类对宇宙的认识。

paragraphs.en: At issue is the TMT’s planned location on Mauna Kea, a dormant volcano worshiped by some Hawaiians as the piko, that connects the Hawaiian Islands to the heavens. But Mauna Kea is also home to some of the world’s most powerful telescopes. Rested in the Pacific Ocean, Mauna Kea’s peak rises above the bulk of our planet’s dense atmosphere, where conditions allow telescopes to obtain images of unsurpassed clarity.
paragraphs.zh: 争议在于，三十米望远镜计划建在莫纳克亚山上。这是一座休眠火山，一些夏威夷人将其奉为连接夏威夷群岛与上天的“皮科”，即脐带。然而，莫纳克亚山也坐落着一些世界上最强大的望远镜。莫纳克亚山位于太平洋中，其山顶高出地球稠密大气层的主体部分，那里的条件使望远镜能够获取无与伦比的清晰图像。

paragraphs.en: Opposition to telescopes on Mauna Kea is nothing new. A small but vocal group of Hawaiians and environmentalists have long viewed their presence as disrespect for sacred land and a painful reminder of the occupation of what was once a sovereign nation.
paragraphs.zh: 反对在莫纳克亚山上设置望远镜，并不是什么新鲜事。长期以来，一小群夏威夷人和环保人士虽人数不多，却积极发声，认为这些望远镜的存在是对圣地的不敬，也让人痛苦地想起这个曾经拥有主权的国家遭到占领的历史。

paragraphs.en: Some blame for the current controversy belongs to astronomers. In their eagerness to build bigger telescopes, they forgot that science is not the only way of understanding the world. They did not always prioritize the protection of Mauna Kea’s fragile ecosystems or its holiness to the island’s inhabitants. Hawaiian culture is not a relic of the past; it is a living culture undergoing a renaissance today.
paragraphs.zh: 天文学家应为当前的争议承担部分责任。他们急于建造更大的望远镜，却忘记了科学并不是理解世界的唯一途径。他们并不总是优先保护莫纳克亚山脆弱的生态系统，也未必把它对岛上居民的神圣意义放在首位。夏威夷文化并非过去留下的遗迹；它是一种鲜活的文化，如今正经历复兴。

paragraphs.en: Yet science has a cultural history, too, with roots going back to the dawn of civilization. The same curiosity to find what lies beyond the horizon that first brought early Polynesians to Hawaii’s shores inspires astronomers today to explore the heavens. Calls to disassemble all telescopes on Mauna Kea or to ban future development there ignore the reality that astronomy and Hawaiian culture both seek to answer big questions about who we are, where we come from and where we are going. Perhaps that is why we explore the starry skies, as if answering a primal calling to know ourselves and our true ancestral homes.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，科学也拥有自身的文化历史，其根源可以追溯到文明的曙光时期。最初驱使早期波利尼西亚人来到夏威夷海岸的，是对地平线之外世界的好奇；如今，激励天文学家探索天空的，也是同样的好奇心。有人呼吁拆除莫纳克亚山上所有望远镜，或禁止未来在那里进行开发，这忽视了一个事实：天文学和夏威夷文化都在试图回答有关我们是谁、来自哪里、将去往何方的重大问题。或许这正是我们探索星空的原因，仿佛是在回应一种原初的召唤，去认识我们自己，以及我们真正的祖先家园。

paragraphs.en: The astronomy community is making compromises to change its use of Mauna Kea. The TMT site was chosen to minimize the telescope’s visibility around the island and to avoid archaeological and environmental impact. To limit the number of telescopes on Mauna Kea, old ones will be removed at the end of their lifetimes and their sites returned to a natural state. There is no reason why everyone cannot be welcomed on Mauna Kea to embrace their cultural heritage and to study the stars.
paragraphs.zh: 天文学界正在作出妥协，改变其使用莫纳克亚山的方式。三十米望远镜的选址，旨在尽量降低从岛上各处看到望远镜的可能性，并避免对考古遗存和环境造成影响。为限制莫纳克亚山上望远镜的数量，旧望远镜在使用寿命结束后将被拆除，其所在地将恢复自然状态。没有理由不欢迎所有人来到莫纳克亚山，认同和珍视自己的文化遗产，并研究星空。
